title: # [Power Display] External DDC/CI monitor disappears after another PC reboots.
summary: The supplied transition and report justify a focused recovery reproduction; active-path loss must be separated from cached discovery.

evidence: The laptop uses HDMI to a Lenovo P27q-30; another PC uses DisplayPort, with monitor input selection set to Auto. Rebooting that PC repeatedly removes the Lenovo from Power Display CLI output until PowerToys restarts.

The reporter already supplies monitor/GPU identity, VCP 0x60 input values, unsuccessful DisplaySwitch/PnP/graphics-reset attempts, and a diagnostic ZIP. PnP presence is not proof of an active display path.
The report records rescans with no external target after some transitions and successful Lenovo discovery after restart; it also records successful device-change recovery earlier in the session.
judgment.recommended_action: Route a bounded full-design investigation after manual-refresh versus restart reproduction; use the existing report first.
judgment.rationale: Detailed topology, repeated steps, recovery control and diagnostics make another generic evidence request unnecessary. A precise recovery boundary remains unconfirmed.

fix_assessment.rationale: A conditional recovery correction is justified for investigation; the cited related issues do not provide concrete coverage.

proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a rescan observes an inactive HDMI path and the cached CLI inventory is not refreshed after that path returns. The supplied report shows actual rescans with zero external targets, so a generic stale-handle claim is not established.
proposed_fixes.title: Power Display input-transition recovery investigation
verification: Repeat the reported HDMI/DisplayPort transition, including repeated remote reboots and delayed HDMI recovery.
Verify CLI list and input switching recover without restarting PowerToys once the monitor is controllable.
Check genuine unplug, sleep/wake and failed DDC probes do not leave stale writable entries or unbounded retries.

confidence.rationale: The source identifies a plausible boundary, but this pass did not reproduce the failing transition. The accompanying diagnostic action distinguishes competing explanations.

plan: Reproduce the input-auto/remote-reboot sequence and correlate active display paths, watcher events and CLI snapshot contents.
Compare manual refresh with full process restart after HDMI is active.
If recovery is missed, design a bounded settled-path rescan/invalidation mechanism; if discovery still omits an active target, investigate that inventory boundary instead.
Preserve inactive/removed-monitor semantics and safe hardware-handle lifetime; do not simply retain unavailable monitors as connected.

initial_investigation: Read the full issue, attachment and related #48977/#47623 descriptions. Those concern duplicate/first-monitor enumeration and do not establish this input-switch transition as the same bug.
Inspected Power Display classification/discovery logs around missing-target and successful rediscovery states; a blanket claim that discovery never ran would contradict the report.

DisplayConfigInventory.cs queries only active display paths; MonitorManager rebuilds its collection from that inventory. DeviceWatcher ignores property-only updates, while add/remove and display-on events schedule rescans.

The current CLI request handler serves the app monitor snapshot rather than forcing fresh hardware enumeration on list. A stale snapshot and a temporarily inactive HDMI path are competing explanations.
History includes #47876 display-wake rescan support; no exact covering fix or fork implementation appeared in the fetched links/searches.
Reassessed the complete current issue discussion and timeline, including the latest maintainer labels. Label changes alone do not satisfy unanswered evidence requests or prove a repair.
inferences: A recovery notification or snapshot invalidation gap is plausible, but the report does not prove a stale physical handle or an always-missed rescan.

information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer reproduction: keep the reported dual-input topology, capture CLI list before/after the other PC reboot, return the monitor to HDMI, invoke Power Display refresh and compare with Windows active-display state.
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates missed recovery notification/cached inventory from persistent discovery failure or an actually inactive path.
information_gaps.information: Whether a manual Power Display refresh after HDMI becomes active restores the missing Lenovo without restarting PowerToys.

actions.label: Approve conditional Power Display input-transition recovery investigation plan

reproduce.expected_result: Once HDMI is active and DDC/CI is available, Power Display rediscovers the monitor and input switching works without a process restart.
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.102.3001 on the reporting topology; compare current source separately.
setup: Use a laptop over HDMI and another PC over DisplayPort to the same DDC/CI monitor with input Auto; enable Power Display.
Use Lenovo P27q-30 if available, or record the model/firmware and input auto-switch behavior for an equivalent setup.
prerequisites: Use non-sensitive test data and preserve the original configuration before changing it.
steps: 1. Confirm both laptop displays in PowerToys.PowerDisplay.Cli.exe list.
2. Leave the laptop running while the other PC uses DisplayPort, then reboot that PC.
3. Record CLI list and Windows active-display state, not just PnP presence.
4. Return the monitor to HDMI, invoke Power Display refresh, and compare CLI output before restarting PowerToys.
5. If still missing, restart PowerToys as the reporter control and compare discovery classification and watcher events.
reproduce.title: Verify the reported Power Display transition
